note: Work: 16. Employment (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, Cap. 346 (Laws of Barbados, L.R.O. 2002, as the Labour Department publishes it): a 'child' is under 16 (Act 2001-5); no child may be employed in any industrial undertaking or ship (s. 11), work between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. in any undertaking (s. 13), or, being of compulsory school age, be employed during school hours (s. 14). The reading: 16 is the age from which a person may be employed in general; below it the Act bars industrial work, ships, night work and school hours, not every job. Performers: free, the reading being that the Act's bars on a child don't reach work outside industry, ships, night and school hours, and it names no permit for performing; the night bar (6 p.m. to 7 a.m.) and school hours still hold for a child performer, and aren't held. Family undertakings and technical schools are outside Part IV (s. 12). Majority: 18. Minors Act, Cap. 215 (L.R.O. 1985, as the Parliament of Barbados's statutes site publishes it; an OCR'd scan whose word 'eighteen' in s. 3(1) is garbled, read with the next line): a person attains full age at 18 instead of 21, from 23 May 1974; a minor is one not of full age. Service: none. Defence Act, Cap. 159 (L.R.O. 1985 and 2007 pages): the regular Force enlists a person who desires to enlist, understands the notice and wishes to be enlisted (s. 19); under 18 only with a parent's written consent.
